Short Description: Pioneered accelerated computing and manufacturing of advanced chips, systems, and software for AI factories. The core foundation of their company is their compute and networking power, which are used for AI solutions, graphics, healthcare, data centers, etc.
Revenue Exposure %: ~89.70% Direct (Data Center/Generative AI segment: $193.7B of $215.9B FY2026 total revenue); ~100% Total AI Ecosystem exposure
Moat Notes: Architectural Lock-In: CUDA has spent almost 20 years embedding itself into ML toolchains, kernels, and pipelines, making NVIDIA hardware the default fast path for most frameworks. Ecosystem Dominance: NVIDIA sells a full stack (GPUs, CUDA software, and NVLink/InfiniBand networking), giving it an estimated ~80%+ share of the data-center AI accelerator market. Switching Costs: Migrating off CUDA means rewriting code, retraining teams, and rebuilding pipelines — a months-long effort with real performance risk. Scarcity/Bottleneck Position: NVIDIA has locked up the majority of TSMC CoWoS advanced-packaging capacity through 2027, throttling every competitor's ability to scale.
Growth Catalysts: Backlog Growth: ~$1 trillion in Blackwell/Rubin orders through 2027. Hyperscaler & Sovereign AI Commitments: Big-four hyperscaler capex roughly doubled to $725B in 2026, sovereign AI revenue tripled to $30B+. Product Cycle Timing: Annual Hopper→Blackwell→Rubin cadence continues with Rubin shipping H2 2026.
Risk Notes: Concentration: Two customers alone made up 22% and 14% of FY2026 revenue. Cyclicality: Long lead times and non-cancellable orders have already caused supply/demand mismatches. Execution Risk: Annual architecture cadence raises odds of transition stumbles.

Short Description: Dell designs, builds, and sells the Dell AI Factory, PowerEdge AI-optimized servers, networking, and storage bundled with NVIDIA and other partner technology, as full-stack, on-prem/hybrid AI infrastructure for enterprises and cloud/service providers.
Revenue Exposure %: ~22% Direct (AI-optimized server revenue ~$25B of $113.5B FY2026 total revenue)
Moat Notes: Architectural Lock-In: Low. Dell is a systems integrator/reseller of NVIDIA silicon, not a proprietary chip/software architecture owner. Ecosystem Dominance: Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA positions Dell as the top-ranked AI infrastructure provider by unit share. Switching Costs: Moderate, driven by existing enterprise IT relationships and financing. Scarcity/Bottleneck Position: None of its own — Dell is itself supply-constrained by GPU, DRAM/NAND, and CPU allocation.
Growth Catalysts: Backlog Growth: FY2026 AI server backlog hit a record $43B. Hyperscaler & Sovereign AI Commitments: Enterprise AI server orders growing faster than CSP orders. Product Cycle Timing: FY2027 guide ~$50B AI server revenue tied to NVIDIA Vera Rubin-based systems.
Risk Notes: Concentration: Heavy dependence on a single external chip supplier (NVIDIA) for AI-optimized servers. Cyclicality: AI server business described as complex and lumpy, tied to customer data-center/power readiness. Execution Risk: Targets only mid-single-digit operating margins on AI servers even as segment scales rapidly.

Short Description: Designs and assembles liquid- and air-cooled AI server racks built on NVIDIA GB300 NVL72/HGX B300 and AMD MI350/355 platforms under its Data Center Building Block Solutions architecture for hyperscalers, sovereigns, and neoclouds.
Revenue Exposure %: ~80%+ Direct (AI GPU-related platforms contributed more than 80% of Q3 FY2026 revenue); effectively majority of total business
Moat Notes: Architectural Lock-In: Modular, open-standard DCBBS architecture speeds customization for liquid-cooled, high-density racks. Ecosystem Dominance: First-to-market advantage with each new NVIDIA/AMD GPU generation; ~9% of NVIDIA's total revenue reflects deep design-partner integration. Switching Costs: Comparatively shallow — low switching costs and intense price competition from Dell, HPE, and other ODMs. Scarcity/Bottleneck Position: None structural; competes primarily on speed-to-market.
Growth Catalysts: Backlog Expansion: Received more than $60B in new orders in fiscal Q4 2026 alone. Hyperscaler & Sovereign AI Commitments: Orders spanning hyperscalers, sovereigns, and neoclouds. Product Cycle Timing: NVIDIA GB300 NVL72/HGX B300 and AMD MI350/355 platform ramps.
Risk Notes: Concentration: Heavily concentrated in a small number of very large hyperscaler/neocloud orders. Cyclicality: Prior-quarter operating cash outflow of $6.6B; cash fell from $4.09B to $1.29B. Execution Risk: Ongoing independent Board review of alleged export-control issues; history of accounting/reporting scrutiny (2024 delinquent filings).

Short Description: Enterprise IT infrastructure company delivering AI-optimized servers and hybrid cloud (GreenLake) platforms, and — following its $14B acquisition of Juniper Networks — AI-native networking equipment for enterprises, sovereigns, and service providers.
Revenue Exposure %: ~50% Direct (Server segment ~$17.4B FY2025 + Cloud & AI segment $7.7B Q2 FY2026); broader Networking segment (Juniper-driven) also AI-linked
Moat Notes: Architectural Lock-In: GreenLake hybrid-cloud platform and full-stack compute + networking + storage integration lock enterprise and sovereign customers into multi-year infrastructure commitments. Ecosystem Dominance: Extended partnership with NVIDIA; $14B Juniper acquisition makes HPE #2 networking player behind Cisco. Switching Costs: Sovereign and enterprise customers commit to multi-year AI system deployments with long lead times. Scarcity/Bottleneck Position: AI server sales pipeline described as multiples of backlog.
Growth Catalysts: Backlog Expansion: AI server backlog climbed to nearly $6B (Q2 FY2026). Hyperscaler & Sovereign AI Commitments: More than 60% of cumulative AI orders since Q1 FY2023 from sovereign and enterprise customers. Product Cycle Timing: FY2027 framework targets non-GAAP operating margin of 12-16%.
Risk Notes: Concentration: AI server shipment timing sensitive to a relatively small number of large sovereign customers. Cyclicality: Server segment operating margin has swung 8-12% by quarter depending on mix and pricing. Execution Risk: Large-scale Juniper Networks integration ($14B acquisition) carries ongoing execution risk; FY2025 GAAP margin was negative on acquisition charges.

Short Description: Develops high-speed connectivity solutions for hyperscale AI data centers. Products include Active Electrical Cables (AECs), SerDes IP, retimers, optical DSPs, and connectivity chips that enable low-power, high-bandwidth networking for AI clusters and cloud infrastructure.
Revenue Exposure %: Estimated ~70-80% Direct (majority of revenue derived from hyperscale AI connectivity products, primarily AECs for GPU clusters)
Moat Notes: Architectural Lock-In: AEC technology designed specifically for AI rack-scale networking; high-speed SerDes IP integrated into customer silicon platforms. Ecosystem Dominance: Leading supplier of low-power AECs for hyperscale AI clusters with strong design wins. Switching Costs: Connectivity components require extensive qualification within AI server platforms; once qualified, customers typically retain suppliers across multiple product generations. Scarcity/Bottleneck Position: One of few suppliers capable of delivering ultra-low-power 800G and emerging 1.6T connectivity solutions.
Growth Catalysts: Backlog/Order Growth: Strong demand for AECs driven by rapid deployment of AI GPU clusters. Hyperscaler & Sovereign AI Commitments: Continued AI infrastructure investment by major hyperscalers; Ethernet-based AI networking adoption. Product Cycle Timing: Expansion of 800G AEC deployments; transition toward 1.6T; growth in PCIe Gen6 and next-generation AI networking.
Risk Notes: Concentration: Heavy dependence on a limited number of hyperscale cloud customers. Cyclicality: Revenue tied to AI infrastructure spending cycles and cloud capital expenditures. Execution Risk: Maintaining technology leadership in high-speed connectivity; scaling manufacturing; competition from optical interconnect and larger semiconductor vendors.

Short Description: Designs semiconductor solutions for AI data centers, including Tomahawk and Jericho Ethernet switch silicon, custom AI accelerator chips (XPUs) co-developed with hyperscalers, and networking/connectivity silicon for AI clusters. The 2023 VMware acquisition extends Broadcom into enterprise infrastructure software.
Revenue Exposure %: Estimated ~45-55% Direct (30-35% from AI networking silicon + 10-20% from custom AI accelerators/XPUs); remaining revenue from broadband, wireless, storage, VMware software
Moat Notes: Architectural Lock-In: Tomahawk and Jericho Ethernet switching architectures widely deployed inside hyperscale AI fabrics; custom ASIC development tightly integrated into hyperscaler AI infrastructure roadmaps. Ecosystem Dominance: Leading merchant Ethernet switch silicon supplier; deep relationships with Google, Meta, Microsoft, Oracle Cloud. VMware software platform increases enterprise infrastructure stickiness. Switching Costs: Hardware qualification cycles are lengthy; software stack and AI cluster architectures optimized around Broadcom silicon; multi-year custom ASIC engagements create long-term customer dependence. Scarcity/Bottleneck Position: One of only a handful of companies capable of delivering cutting-edge AI networking silicon at hyperscale.
Growth Catalysts: Backlog/Order Growth: Multi-year AI infrastructure commitments from hyperscalers. Hyperscaler & Sovereign AI Commitments: AI infrastructure expansion across Microsoft, Google, Meta, Oracle, Amazon, and sovereign AI initiatives. Product Cycle Timing: Ramp of Tomahawk 6 (102.4 Tbps); growth in custom AI XPUs; expansion of 800G and future 1.6T Ethernet.
Risk Notes: Concentration: Significant revenue concentration among a small number of hyperscale cloud customers. Cyclicality: Dependent on hyperscaler capital expenditure cycles and enterprise infrastructure spending. Execution Risk: Maintaining leadership in merchant Ethernet silicon; delivering increasingly complex custom AI ASIC programs; VMware integration and execution risks.

Short Description: Provides networking infrastructure, including Ethernet switches, routers, and networking software for enterprises, service providers, and cloud providers. Its platforms support AI data center connectivity and AI workloads.
Revenue Exposure %: 8-9% Direct (AI Factory hardware/silicon deployments); ~18-20% Total AI Ecosystem exposure (includes automated campus networks, enterprise security integration, Splunk data analytics, and full-stack software management)
Moat Notes: Architectural Lock-In: Integrated networking architecture built around Cisco Silicon One, IOS XE/NX-OS, and unified networking, security, and observability platforms. Ecosystem Dominance: Global leader in enterprise networking with an extensive installed base, broad partner ecosystem, and long-standing relationships with enterprises and cloud operators. Switching Costs: High cost and operational complexity of replacing installed networking infrastructure, retraining IT teams, and migrating configurations and security policies. Scarcity/Bottleneck Position: Supplier of AI-ready Ethernet networking platforms and high-capacity data center switching infrastructure.
Growth Catalysts: Backlog/Order Growth: AI infrastructure orders expected to reach $9B in FY2026; networking product orders accelerating. Hyperscaler & Sovereign AI Commitments: Continued expansion of AI networking with hyperscalers, plus growing AI pipeline from neocloud, sovereign, and enterprise customers. Product Cycle Timing: Ramp of Silicon One, 800G optics, AI Ethernet networking, and next-generation campus networking platforms.
Risk Notes: Concentration: Dependence on enterprise, service provider, and cloud customers; reduced IT spending by large customers may negatively impact revenue. Cyclicality: Business affected by macroeconomic conditions, enterprise IT spending cycles, government budgets, and fluctuations in customer capital expenditure. Execution Risk: Ability to successfully execute AI networking strategy, introduce new products, integrate acquisitions, and compete in rapidly evolving networking and AI infrastructure markets.

Short Description: Provides cloud networking solutions for data centers and cloud computing environments. Offers high-performance Ethernet switches, routers, and the Extensible Operating System (EOS) for next-generation data center networks.
Revenue Exposure %: 31-33% Direct (AI data center fabrics/GPU clustering); ~53-56% Total AI Ecosystem exposure (includes automated front-end management, CloudVision software automation, deep telemetry routing, and enterprise hybrid cloud networks)
Moat Notes: Architectural Lock-In: Cloud-native networking architecture built on EOS, enabling consistent automation, programmability, and large-scale data center operations. Ecosystem Dominance: Leading provider of high-speed Ethernet networking for hyperscale cloud providers and AI data centers, with deep integration across cloud networking environments. Switching Costs: High migration costs due to EOS-based automation workflows, network configurations, and operational processes embedded in large-scale cloud infrastructure. Scarcity/Bottleneck Position: Specialized provider of ultra-high-performance Ethernet switches critical for AI clusters, GPU interconnects, and hyperscale AI networking infrastructure.
Growth Catalysts: Backlog/Order Growth: Strong AI-driven cloud networking demand with continued revenue growth from hyperscale AI data center deployments. Hyperscaler & Sovereign AI Commitments: Ongoing infrastructure expansion by Microsoft, Meta, Alphabet, Oracle, and other cloud providers. Product Cycle Timing: Continued adoption of high-speed 400G/800G Ethernet networking and AI cluster interconnect solutions.
Risk Notes: Concentration: Significant reliance on a limited number of hyperscale cloud customers; changes in purchasing patterns could materially affect revenue. Cyclicality: Demand depends on cloud infrastructure investment cycles, hyperscaler capital expenditures, and broader economic conditions. Execution Risk: Continued growth depends on delivering next-generation Ethernet platforms, maintaining technology leadership, managing supply chain, and responding to intense competition.

Short Description: Diversified power management company; supplies electrical distribution, switchgear, and UPS systems, and via the Boyd Thermal acquisition, liquid cooling equipment for hyperscale AI data centers, plus a co-developed grid-to-chip platform (Beam Rubin DSX) with NVIDIA.
Revenue Exposure %: ~21% Direct (Data Centers & Distributed IT end market per FY2026 outlook disclosed on Q4 2025 earnings call)
Moat Notes: Architectural Lock-In: Multi-year electrical infrastructure contracts; once a facility's power architecture is designed around Eaton equipment, replacing it is costly and disruptive. Ecosystem Dominance: NVIDIA co-engineering relationship (Beam Rubin DSX) embeds Eaton in reference designs replicated across hyperscale builds; Boyd Thermal acquisition ($9.5B) extends dominance into liquid cooling. Switching Costs: High switching cost once designed into a facility's electrical architecture, reinforced by long lead times and compatibility requirements. Scarcity/Bottleneck Position: Manufacturing capacity constrained industry-wide; Eaton investing $1.5B+ in capacity through 2026.
Growth Catalysts: Backlog Expansion: Electrical Americas backlog $13.2B (+31% YoY); total company backlog >$19B. Hyperscaler & Sovereign AI Commitments: 17 GW of planned data-center capacity commitments for 2026; NVIDIA co-engineering relationship. Public Infrastructure Funding Super-Cycle: $3T+ North American megaproject pipeline (866 projects announced); Eaton wins ~40%. Margin Expansion: Boyd Thermal sales targeted at $1.7B in 2026 (+100%+ YoY).
Risk Notes: Concentration: Growing reliance on hyperscaler/mega-project spend for backlog growth. Cyclicality: Margin compression from capacity-ramp costs and temporary negative price/cost. Execution Risk: Rising debt/goodwill from Boyd Thermal + Ultra PCS deals; integration/leverage risk.

Short Description: Energy equipment company that generates, transfers, and manages electricity; its Power segment (gas turbines) and Electrification segment (grid transformers, switchgear, substations) supply the baseload power and interconnection equipment AI data centers require.
Revenue Exposure %: Estimated ~15-20% Direct (data-center share of gas-turbine backlog ~20% of 116 GW, and Electrification data-center orders >$5B YTD 2026); Total AI Ecosystem Exposure: Broader Power and Electrification segments (backlog $176B) benefit indirectly, not separately broken out
Moat Notes: Architectural Lock-In: Decades-long utility relationships anchor recurring services/MRO revenue tied to an installed base of turbines. Ecosystem Dominance: Duopoly-scale heavy-duty gas turbine manufacturing alongside Siemens Energy/Mitsubishi; HA-class turbine efficiency (>64% combined-cycle) is the reference technology. Switching Costs: Once a utility or data-center operator commits to GE Vernova turbines, ongoing servicing, parts, and technical support create strong incumbency. Scarcity/Bottleneck Position: Global heavy-duty gas turbine capacity sold out into ~2031; Electrification equipment (transformers/switchgear) faces its own global supply bottleneck.
Growth Catalysts: Backlog Expansion: Total company backlog $176B (Q2 2026); management targets $200B by 2027; turbine backlog grew to 116 GW. Hyperscaler & Sovereign AI Commitments: Revenue per GW of data-center capacity ~$300M, could grow 2-3x as newer grid products commercialize. Public Infrastructure Funding Super-Cycle: FY2026 revenue guidance raised twice, most recently to $45.5B-$46.5B. Margin Expansion: Adjusted EBITDA margin improvement expected as Wind segment drag narrows.
Risk Notes: Concentration: Reliance on continued utility and hyperscaler capex commitments to convert backlog into revenue. Cyclicality: Wind segment remains a persistent drag (Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $275M); manufacturing capacity is the binding constraint on growth. Execution Risk: Q2 2026 adjusted EPS missed consensus despite a revenue beat; high valuation multiple leaves limited room for AI capex slowdown or further Wind stumble.

Short Description: Global energy-technology company supplying gas and steam turbines (Gas Services), high-voltage grid equipment and HVDC transmission links (Grid Technologies), and industrial electrification that underpin AI data-center power and grid interconnection, alongside its Siemens Gamesa wind business.
Revenue Exposure %: Estimated ~15-20% Direct (Grid Technologies data-center/hyperscaler-linked orders >€21B of €58.9B FY2025 orders, and Gas Services AI-datacenter-linked turbine deliveries); Total AI Ecosystem Exposure: Broader Grid Technologies + Gas Services (contributing to €138B backlog) benefit from AI-driven grid modernization demand, not separately broken out
Moat Notes: Architectural Lock-In: Long-term service contracts on installed gas-turbine/grid-equipment base create stable recurring revenue. Ecosystem Dominance: One of a small number of global suppliers (with GE Vernova, Mitsubishi, Hitachi Energy) capable of heavy-duty turbines and grid equipment at scale; Grid Technologies posted highest quarterly revenue on record Q4 FY2025. Switching Costs: Multi-year delivery/service contracts; transformer lead times stretched from 12 to 48-60 months industry-wide. Scarcity/Bottleneck Position: Record €138B backlog; industry-wide electrical-steel (GOES) supply constraints reinforce incumbency.
Growth Catalysts: Backlog Expansion: Record €138B backlog, order intake €58.9B, book-to-bill 1.36 in Q4 FY2025. Hyperscaler & Sovereign AI Commitments: Grid Technologies US orders above €21B, reflecting hyperscaler and utility grid-interconnection demand. Public Infrastructure Funding Super-Cycle: Broader grid modernization and electrification investment cycle across US, European, and global utility markets. Margin Expansion: Profit before special items grew more than 6x YoY to €2,355M, beating original 3-5% outlook.
Risk Notes: Concentration: Growth increasingly reliant on large hyperscaler and utility grid-interconnection orders converting backlog on schedule. Cyclicality: Siemens Gamesa wind business remains a turnaround story with historical quality issues and prior negative profit guidance, a persistent drag on group profitability. Execution Risk: Premium valuation multiples and elevated execution risk in scaling gas-turbine and grid-equipment manufacturing capacity (new US facilities in Mississippi and North Carolina).

Short Description: Largest operator of nuclear power plants in the US; supplies firm, 24/7 carbon-free baseload power to hyperscalers via long-term PPAs, and, following its Calpine acquisition, natural gas and geothermal generation.
Revenue Exposure %: Estimated ~4-5% Direct (signed hyperscaler PPA capacity: 2,336 MW across Meta 1,121 MW + Microsoft 835 MW + Calpine/CyrusOne 380 MW, relative to combined ~55-60 GW fleet post-Calpine); Total AI Ecosystem Exposure: Over 5,650 MW of total long-term clean-energy agreements signed, growing share tied to AI/data-center demand
Moat Notes: Architectural Lock-In: 20-year PPAs with hyperscalers tied to specific plants lock in decades of contracted revenue. Ecosystem Dominance: Owns roughly one-quarter of all US nuclear reactors; only operator able to offer firm, 24/7 carbon-free baseload power at the multi-GW scale hyperscalers seek. Switching Costs: Once a hyperscaler signs a 20-year PPA tied to a specific plant, there is no practical way to switch power suppliers without abandoning the underlying infrastructure investment. Scarcity/Bottleneck Position: Existing US nuclear capacity essentially fixed near-term; new nuclear construction takes a decade or more.
Growth Catalysts: Backlog Expansion: Over 5,650 MW of long-term clean-energy agreements signed; ~1 GW of nuclear uprates planned alongside $3.9B capex. Hyperscaler & Sovereign AI Commitments: 20-year PPAs with Meta (1,121 MW), Microsoft (835 MW), and new 380 MW Calpine/CyrusOne data-center agreement. Public Infrastructure Funding: DOE approved $1B loan guarantee to advance Crane Clean Energy Center restart; NRC approved extended operating licenses. Margin Expansion: Calpine acquisition expanded fleet to ~55-60 GW; management guides 2026 adjusted EPS of $11.00-$12.00 (+17-28% YoY) with 20%+ CAGR target through 2029.
Risk Notes: Concentration: Revenue increasingly reliant on a small number of very large, multi-decade hyperscaler PPAs converting into realized cash flow. Cyclicality: GAAP operating income fell 29.1% YoY in FY2025 on unfavorable nuclear production-tax-credit portfolio results and mark-to-market hedge losses. Execution Risk: $16.4B Calpine acquisition adds ~$12.7B of assumed debt and integration risk; Crane Clean Energy Center restart subject to NRC safety/environmental review and additional permitting.

Short Description: Provides liquid and air cooling infrastructure for data centers — including Coolant Distribution Units (CDUs), chillers, and computer-room air handlers designed specifically for high-density AI racks.
Revenue Exposure %: Estimated ~75% Direct (data center customer revenue share, per analyst commentary); Total AI Ecosystem Exposure: ~85-90% including hyperscale data centers, colocation facilities, and adjacent power/thermal infrastructure
Moat Notes: Architectural Lock-In: Once cooling architecture is integrated into a data center's building management systems, switching suppliers becomes costly. Ecosystem Dominance: Market leader in liquid cooling with 11.3% global share. Switching Costs: Long-term service contracts tied to proprietary CoolChip CDU platform. Scarcity/Bottleneck Position: $15B backlog reflects constrained industry capacity for liquid cooling demand.
Growth Catalysts: Backlog Expansion: $15B project backlog covering 12-18 months of forward revenue. Hyperscaler & Sovereign AI Commitments: Americas hyperscale and colocation demand cited as primary growth driver. Product Cycle Timing: Liquid cooling TAM expanding from $4.8B (2025) to $27.1B by 2035. Margin Expansion: Management targets operating margins expanding toward 25% by 2029.
Risk Notes: Concentration: Reliance on a small number of hyperscaler/colocation customers. Cyclicality: Bear case centers on potential hyperscaler capex pauses. Execution Risk: Component supply bottlenecks during production ramp; premium valuation leaves little room for missteps.

Short Description: Legacy thermal management company that pivoted into data center liquid cooling, recently creating a standalone Data Centers division and spinning off its legacy automotive segment.
Revenue Exposure %: Estimated ~25% Direct based on Data Center Cooling segment (% of FY2025 total net sales, up from 4% prior year); ~56% Total Climate Solutions segment exposure (includes data center cooling + commercial HVAC&R, FY2025)
Moat Notes: Architectural Lock-In: Custom liquid cooling systems built into new hyperscale capacity investments (Franklin, Wisconsin plant). Ecosystem Dominance: Recently elevated data center cooling to a standalone division. Switching Costs: Long lead times (18+ months) industry-wide favor incumbent suppliers. Scarcity/Bottleneck Position: US-centric manufacturing model differentiates amid global supply constraints.
Growth Catalysts: Backlog Expansion: $180M order win from a leading AI infrastructure developer drove a 102% YoY sales surge. Hyperscaler & Sovereign AI Commitments: Data center cooling revenue grew from 4% to 25% of total net sales in FY2025. Product Cycle Timing: Data center cooling market projected at 11.8% CAGR through 2030. Margin Expansion: Raised FY2026 guidance for 20-25% net sales growth.
Risk Notes: Concentration: Heavy reliance on continued AI/hyperscaler capex cycle. Cyclicality: Recent margin compression from supply chain disruptions and tariffs. Execution Risk: Risk of overbuilding capacity if AI demand normalizes faster than expected.

Short Description: Swedish OEM that designs, builds, and services cooling systems for data centers through its Data Center Technologies (DCT) business area, offering both air and liquid cooling.
Revenue Exposure %: Estimated ~40% Direct based on Data Center Technologies (DCT) segment (~SEK 6B of ~SEK 15B total group net sales, FY2025); ~40-45% Total AI Ecosystem exposure (DCT segment plus adjacent AI-driven demand)
Moat Notes: Architectural Lock-In: Geoclima Circlemiser chiller platform built for mission-critical, high-density environments. Ecosystem Dominance: OEM status — designs, builds, and services cooling systems across full lifecycle. Switching Costs: Long-term service and commissioning contracts tied to delivered infrastructure. Scarcity/Bottleneck Position: Global production footprint across 30+ countries provides supply resilience.
Growth Catalysts: Backlog Expansion: Order intake increased 32% YoY, driven by DCT demand. Hyperscaler & Sovereign AI Commitments: Secured $183M AI cooling order for a US data center (2026). Product Cycle Timing: DCT margin expected to improve in H2 2026 as tariff effects ease. Margin Expansion: Management targets improved Group profitability in 2026 supported by DCT backlog.
Risk Notes: Concentration: Revenue lumpiness from reliance on large individual hyperscale orders. Cyclicality: SEK currency exposure and temporary tariff headwinds. Execution Risk: Product transition costs and dual-site cost pressures during capacity scaling.

Short Description: Electrical connection and protection company whose Thermal Management (liquid cooling) and Enclosures segments supply power distribution, electrical protection, and direct-to-chip/liquid cooling systems for AI data centers and grid infrastructure.
Revenue Exposure %: ~26% Direct (data-center revenue reached approximately $1.0B of $3.9B total FY2025 sales, up from ~$600M in FY2024); Total AI Ecosystem Exposure: Broader infrastructure vertical (data center + power-utility modernization) reached ~45% of total FY2025 sales
Moat Notes: Architectural Lock-In: Liquid cooling and electrical protection systems designed into a data center's power/thermal architecture at construction, making mid-project vendor swaps disruptive and costly. Ecosystem Dominance: Positioned by analysts as a mini Vertiv for liquid cooling and electrical protection in AI data centers; expanding liquid-cooling production capacity with new dedicated facilities. Switching Costs: Multi-year large AI/data-center project awards lock nVent in as incumbent supplier through a facility's full build-out and maintenance cycle. Scarcity/Bottleneck Position: Record $2.3B backlog (~3x year-ago) reflects capacity constraints across the liquid-cooling supply chain.
Growth Catalysts: Backlog Expansion: Record year-end backlog of $2.3B (~3x prior year); Q4 2025 organic orders +~30% driven largely by large AI/data-center projects. Hyperscaler & Sovereign AI Commitments: Data-center revenue reached ~$1.0B in FY2025 from ~$600M in FY2024, driven by large hyperscaler and AI-focused data-center wins. Public Infrastructure Funding Super-Cycle: Power-utility modernization a secondary but growing driver within the infrastructure vertical. Margin Expansion: Adjusted operating income grew 21% in FY2025 to $786M; 2026 guidance calls for 15-18% reported sales growth and 20-24% adjusted EPS growth.
Risk Notes: Concentration: Growing reliance on a relatively small number of very large AI/data-center project orders to sustain backlog growth. Cyclicality: FY2025 margins pressured by ~$55M of inflation including >$40M in tariffs; management forecasts an additional ~$80M of incremental tariffs in 2026. Execution Risk: Portfolio transformation (divesting legacy thermal-management business, acquiring EPG) carries integration risk; capacity-ramp inefficiencies cited as a margin headwind.

Short Description: Partners with NVIDIA to deploy AI Factory digital twin blueprints, using virtual simulations to optimize the design, power, and cooling of gigawatt-scale data centers before physical construction begins.
Revenue Exposure %: 3-4% Direct (data center builds/engineering); ~10-11% Total AI Ecosystem exposure (includes data centers, power/grid tie-ins, cooling water infrastructure, and semiconductor fab facilities)
Moat Notes: Architectural Lock-In: End-to-end multi-year lifecycle contracts spanning master planning, site selection, complex power/water design, permitting, and facility management. Ecosystem Dominance: Premier engineering ranking in global water management, transportation, and advanced life science/semiconductor facilities; full acquisition of PA Consulting adds strategy and digital design integration. Switching Costs: High customer reluctance to change engineering design partners mid-build on multi-billion dollar capital projects with strict regulatory, security, and environmental compliance requirements. Scarcity/Bottleneck Position: Specialized technical workforce for ultra-complex engineering amid structural talent shortages.
Growth Catalysts: Backlog Expansion: Total backlog reached a record $27.0B (+21.7% YoY) with TTM book-to-bill ratio >1.1x. Hyperscaler & Sovereign AI Commitments: Accelerating demand for AI data center builds, grid interconnection, power capacity expansion, and water cooling solutions. Public Infrastructure Legislation: Multi-year funding disbursements from IIJA, CHIPS and Science Act, and sovereign water/energy transition initiatives. Margin Expansion Target: Target of 17%+ Adjusted EBITDA margin by FY2029.
Risk Notes: Concentration: High exposure to government funding priorities, geopolitical budget shifts, and spending cuts across federal/municipal clients. Cyclicality: Exposure to broader macroeconomic downturns, high interest rates, or delays in private hyperscaler and enterprise capital expenditures. Execution Risk: Cost overruns on fixed-price contracts, labor shortages, legal/regulatory liabilities from consolidated JVs, and integration risk from PA Consulting.

Short Description: Provides end-to-end design and construction management for hyperscale AI campuses, currently leading the development of the 500 MW Nostrum Evergreen facility in Spain specifically engineered for high-density AI workloads.
Revenue Exposure %: 3-5% Direct (data center engineering, design, and mission-critical tech builds); ~10-12% Total AI Infrastructure & Facilities Ecosystem (includes data centers, power grid interconnections, water cooling, and high-tech industrial facilities)
Moat Notes: Architectural Lock-In: Multi-year lead consultant, master planner, and program manager for multi-billion-dollar global infrastructure, energy, and facility builds. Ecosystem Dominance: Ranked #1 in global transportation, water, and environmental engineering by ENR; leading advisory presence with federal, state, and municipal agencies globally. Switching Costs: High client reluctance to switch engineering design partners mid-project due to deep regulatory integration, proprietary digital modeling (BIM), and complex permitting compliance. Scarcity/Bottleneck Position: Global scarcity of specialized technical talent capable of complex high-voltage power tie-ins, liquid cooling system design, and zero-carbon grid integration.
Growth Catalysts: Backlog Expansion: Record total backlog of $26.2B (+8% YoY) with strong book-to-burn ratio. Hyperscaler & Sovereign AI Commitments: Accelerating capex deployments from major technology companies requiring power grid expansion, data center engineering, and sustainable water solutions. Public Infrastructure Funding Super-Cycle: Multi-year tailwinds from IIJA, CHIPS and Science Act, and global energy transition mandates. Margin Expansion: Asset-light fee-for-service model aiming for 20%+ segment adjusted margin by FY2028 and 15%+ adjusted EPS CAGR from FY2026 to FY2029.
Risk Notes: Concentration: Significant revenue tied to government agency spending, exposing the company to sovereign debt constraints or political policy shifts. Cyclicality: Exposure to corporate investment cycles, high interest rates, or project timing delays from private sector enterprise clients. Execution Risk: Talent acquisition/retention constraints in specialized engineering roles, project delay liabilities, or legal disputes on legacy contracts.

Short Description: Delivers large-scale engineering and construction for AI infrastructure, recently advancing a $3-4 billion, 480-megawatt data center campus in Kentucky designed to support high-performance computing and artificial intelligence.
Revenue Exposure %: 2-4% Direct (data center EPC engineering and construction management); ~10-15% Total AI Ecosystem exposure (includes hyperscaler data centers, semiconductor fabrication facilities, high-voltage power substations, and advanced technology manufacturing)
Moat Notes: Architectural Lock-In: Full EPC/EPCM program management for multi-billion-dollar global infrastructure, energy, and semiconductor mega-projects. Ecosystem Dominance: Top tier engineering ranking in mining, energy transition, government mission solutions, and advanced industrial facilities.
